title: Generic STL Surface Cutting
overview: Cut a closed STL triangle shell between two user-defined planar sections without using analytic shape definitions. The canonical internal-flow cylinder STL is the first blind-input fixture.
principle: The STL triangles are the sole geometry source. The cutter must not read analytic geometry manifests, primitive parameters, patch indices or shape equations. Inlet and outlet planes are explicit inputs; their normals orient the retained half-spaces and the generated end caps.
architecture: grid/stl_import/reader.py -> grid/stl_import/surface_cut.py -> clipped wall triangles + inlet/outlet caps -> closed STL + checksum-bound region_manifest.json -> mesh-project region artifact copy -> region-aware Gmsh Physical Surfaces (wall/inflow/outflow) -> existing Gmsh-to-CGNS BC mapping.

algorithm: Validate a connected, closed, consistently oriented two-manifold input shell.
Clip each triangle polygon against the inlet and outlet plane half-spaces using signed distances.
Weld clipped vertices and extract one-use boundary edges on each cutting plane.
Require one simple closed loop per plane.
Project each loop into a local plane basis and triangulate it using ear clipping.
Orient inlet and outlet cap triangles outward and combine them with the clipped side surface.
Write a checksum-bound region manifest for wall, inflow and outflow STL artifacts; do not infer regions from analytic geometry.
Copy the manifest and its patch STL files into the writable mesh project when the closed shell is opened in STL to Gmsh.
Create distinct Gmsh Physical Surface groups named wall, inflow and outflow and a fluid_domain Physical Volume.
limitations: One boundary loop per cutting plane.
Plane points and normals are supplied explicitly; automatic endpoint direction estimation is not included.
Gmsh meshing, CGNS BC_t inspection and OneFLOW CFD boundary verification remain manual; pure Python tests do not claim physical boundary correctness.

verification.scope: grid/tests/python/stl_import/test_generic_stl_surface_cut.py; Uses the checked-in cylinder STL as blind triangle input; validates the generated closed shell without consulting its analytic manifest.
grid/tests/python/stl_import/test_generic_stl_surface_cut.py; Exercises two non-parallel planar cuts on the same STL input.
grid/tests/python/stl_import/test_generic_stl_surface_cut.py; Runs the CLI adapter against the blind-input cylinder STL and verifies wall, inlet, outlet, closed-shell STL artifacts and the report.
Also validates region_manifest.json checksums/counts and generated Gmsh Physical Surface declarations without running Gmsh.

execution_boundary.ci: Pure geometry unit tests only. Do not install or invoke Gmsh in CI for mesh-generation validation.
execution_boundary.manual: Run Gmsh from Mesh Generation, inspect the MSH groups, convert to CGNS and confirm BCInflow, BCOutflow and BCWall region counts before running the short OneFLOW CFD smoke test.
